paper.citation: Aranyak Acharyya, Joshua Agterberg, Youngser Park, Carey E. Priebe, Concentration bounds on response-based vector embeddings of black-box generative models, arXiv:2511.08307.
paper.source_version: Retained arXiv v1 transcription used by the January-2026 Quench argument. The June-2026 v2 revision is a separate migration target.

purpose: Compare each retained source result in the 2025 concentration paper with the Lean theorem surface, including source repairs and proof-route replacements.

relation_definitions.exact: The source clause and Lean clause have the same mathematical content, modulo notation/encoding.
relation_definitions.equivalent_encoding: The mathematical content is equivalent, but Lean packages it in a structurally different form.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_hypothesis: Lean assumes less than the source at this clause, so the Lean theorem is stronger here.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_hypothesis: Lean assumes more than the source at this clause; this is a source-fidelity gap unless separately justified.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_conclusion: Lean proves at least the source conclusion and additionally proves a stronger conclusion.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_conclusion: Lean proves less than the source conclusion; this is a source-fidelity gap.
relation_definitions.different_quantifier_encoding: Lean makes an informal/asymptotic quantifier pattern explicit using an equivalent or stronger schedule/event formulation.
relation_definitions.derived_by_composition: No single source-shaped declaration exists, but the source clause follows from a checked composition of cited Lean declarations.
relation_definitions.source_repair: The retained source wording is inconsistent, false, or mismatched with its proof; Lean formalizes the repaired mathematical statement.
relation_definitions.proof_role_replaced: The printed proof-side lemma is not exposed literally; a different formal proof route removes or subsumes its role.
relation_definitions.missing: No Lean theorem surface was found for this source clause.
relation_definitions.supplementary: This Lean result goes beyond the printed source and is recorded for context, not source coverage.

rows.title: Entrywise concentration of the centered CMDS matrix
rows.verdict: GAP exact finite probability constant not exposed
rows.source_claim: For any epsilon>0, every entry of Bhat is within epsilon of B with the displayed finite high-probability bound determined by response covariances.

clauses.source_clause: For any epsilon>0, all entries |Bhat_ii'-B_ii'|<epsilon simultaneously with probability at least 1 - 16 sum gamma_ij/(r m epsilon^2).
clauses.lean_clause: EntrywiseClose plus the response-to-CMDS bridge and growing-response concentration prove the same event shape.

clauses.source_clause: The finite displayed failure-probability constant is exactly the paper expression.
clauses.lean_clause: No single source-facing Lean theorem exposes that exact finite constant; the active bridge uses conservative constants.
clauses.note: The asymptotic paper scale is preserved, but constant-level literal fidelity is not packaged.

clauses.source_clause: For any epsilon > 0, P[|Bhat_ii' - B_ii'| < epsilon for all i,i'] >= 1 - 16 sum gamma_ij / (r m epsilon^2).
clauses.lean_clause: The probability step is now finite and explicit: prob_uniformResponseMeanClose_ge_of_secondMoment gives 1 - N sigma^2 / eta^2 for the response means.
clauses.note: The remaining distance is the response-mean to doubly-centred-entry passage, which carries the factor 16 and the 1/(rm) scaling.

clauses.source_clause: For any eps > 0, P[|Bhat_ii' - B_ii'| < eps for all i,i'] >= 1 - 16 sum gamma_ij / (r m eps^2), with no hypothesis on the scale of the population responses.
clauses.lean_clause: prob_entrywiseClose_lt_paper_bound refutes this; the repair is the entrywise dissimilarity bound already carried by the compiled bridge.
clauses.note: At m = 1 the three competing dissimilarity normalisations coincide, so the refutation is independent of that question.

rows.review: The event shape and response-to-CMDS concentration mechanism are compiled, including the paper-scale n^3/r bookkeeping. The exact finite displayed constant is not exposed by one source-facing theorem.
rows.notes: The active response-to-CMDS bridge works entrywise directly and avoids the former n^2 Frobenius detour. Its constants are intentionally conservative.
rows.next_action: Optionally state the corrected finite bound -- the printed one with the entrywise dissimilarity bound R inserted -- as one source-facing theorem.

rows.title: Spectral-norm rate under r = omega(n^3)
rows.source_claim: Under uniformly bounded response variance and r growing faster than n^3, ||Bhat-B|| is below (n^3/r)^(1/2-delta) with high probability for delta in (0,1/2).

clauses.source_clause: sup gamma_ij=O(1), r=omega(n^3), delta in (0,1/2).
clauses.lean_clause: PaperRate defines ReplicatesDominateCubic and paperDeltaScale=(n^3/r)^(1/2-delta), with the corresponding vanishing concentration ratio.

clauses.source_clause: With high probability ||Bhat-B||_op < (n^3/r)^(1/2-delta).
clauses.lean_clause: Entrywise-to-operator transport plus the paper-scale concentration theorem yields this rate by composition.

rows.review: The literal n^3/r real-power scale, its vanishing under r=omega(n^3), and entrywise-to-operator transport are compiled. The source corollary is assembled rather than wrapped verbatim.
rows.notes: The paper-scale module was added specifically to close the source exponent rather than leave only a generic rate parameter.

rows.title: Eventually fixed embedding rank d
rows.source_claim: For sufficiently large n, rank(B)=d with d fixed.

clauses.source_clause: Eventually rank(B)=d for fixed d.
clauses.lean_clause: The operator theorem uses d<=n, positive leading-d eigenvalue floor, and zero trailing eigenvalues; matrix-side structure uses rank<=d plus the positive floor.
clauses.note: Together these force exactly d positive population eigenvalues.

rows.notes: The rank packaging is more convenient for Gram realization and matrix transport than a bare equality.

rows.title: Compact Riemannian-manifold sufficient condition
rows.source_claim: If model latent points lie on a d-dimensional compact Riemannian manifold and population dissimilarities equal geodesic distances, Assumptions 1 and 2 hold.

clauses.source_clause: Assumption 1 and Assumption 2 hold when every model is associated with a vector on a d-dimensional compact Riemannian manifold whose pairwise geodesic distances equal the population dissimilarities.
clauses.lean_clause: no_eigenvalue_floor_for_const_selection and rank_classicalMDSMatrix_const_eq_zero refute both conclusions for a constant selection meeting the hypothesis.
clauses.note: The hypothesis constrains the ambient manifold; the conclusion constrains the placement of the models within it.

rows.review: No manifold/geodesic sufficient-condition theorem was found in the Acharyya2025 package or its cited foundation modules.
rows.notes: This is the clearest remaining numbered-result coverage gap in the main text.
rows.next_action: If a repair is wanted, formulate a spread condition on the model selection strong enough to keep the doubly centred matrix nondegenerate as n grows, and prove Assumptions 1 and 2 from it.

rows.source_claim: Under r=omega(n^3), bounded response variability, and Assumptions 1--2, there exists an orthogonal alignment W* and the embedding error is bounded by a cubic polynomial in (n^3/r)^(1/2-delta) with high probability. The displayed polynomial upper bound is the source's Equation (2), whose coefficients Assumptions 1 and 2 keep bounded.

clauses.source_clause: r=omega(n^3), uniformly bounded response covariance, Assumptions 1 and 2.
clauses.lean_clause: The statistical RateChain supplies operator perturbation epsilon at the paper scale; ConfigPerturbation assumes only rank/floor/cap and operator closeness.

clauses.source_clause: There exists W* in O(d) aligning estimated and population embeddings.
clauses.lean_clause: exists_isometry_configFrobError_spectralConfig_le produces an inner-product-preserving linear map W on R^d; finite-dimensional real isometry is the orthogonal alignment.

clauses.source_clause: The displayed v1 theorem bounds ||psiHat W*-psi||_{2,infinity}.

clauses.source_clause: The error is bounded by a cubic polynomial in x=(n^3/r)^(1/2-delta).
clauses.lean_clause: configFrobBound has an explicit local linear+quadratic majorant and PaperRate composes it with paperDeltaScale; the result vanishes at the printed scale.
